review: T17 Conformance Harness Reliability Review — Round 1

findings.finding: Makefile verify target delegates to pytest; pytest propagates non-zero exit on failure — PASS for normal pytest flow. However, serialize_with_rust and serialize_with_ts silently return None on subprocess failure; test_rust_serializer_basic and test_ts_serializer_basic gate the assertion with `if result:`, meaning a missing binary produces no assertion failure and the test PASSES with exit 0. This masks toolchain-build failures silently.

action.yml runs `python3 independent_verifier.py` as a composite step with `if: always()` but does NOT check the exit code of that step for overall job failure. The step's exit code propagates naturally for composite actions only when the step itself fails — here the verifier correctly uses sys.exit(), so exit propagation is intact. However, the Makefile `verify` target calls only `make test`, not `make verify-independent`, meaning the independent verifier is never invoked via `make verify`. The action.yml calls it directly as a separate step, which is the intended path — but that step has no `timeout-minutes:` limit.

Makefile verify pipes through `npx playwright test 2>&1`; the pipe does NOT consume the exit code — the `2>&1` redirect does not mask exit codes in bash. Playwright exits non-zero on failure, so this is acceptable. Exit codes appear deterministic.
Makefile verify delegates to pytest. Exit code deterministic.

checks.name: Mutation testing: single-byte fixture change causes loud failure

findings.finding: test_fixture_mutation_detection (test_byte_equivalence.py:101) mutates the in-memory copy of the fixture and asserts that Python's built-in hash() returns different values. Python hash() is non-deterministic across interpreter runs (PYTHONHASHSEED) and is not a cryptographic hash — this test proves nothing about byte-level determinism or serialization sensitivity. The test does not re-run the Rust/TS serializer against the mutated fixture and compare outputs. A byte change to the fixture file on disk would not be detected by this test at all.

test_fixture_mutation_detection (test_full_mode_stub.py:115) checks that `original_sig == mutated_sig` (i.e., the signature field is unchanged after mutating slot) — this assertion always passes since the signature is not derived from slot in stub mode. It does not actually verify that a mutated fixture causes downstream serialization or hash mismatch. The test provides false reassurance.

WASM fixture mutation detection (wasm-equivalence.spec.ts:53) compares JSON.stringify of two in-memory objects with different nonce values. This correctly detects the string inequality but the `hashes_differ` label is misleading — no actual hash is computed. More importantly, the test does not invoke any WASM serialization path; it exercises only JSON.stringify. A byte change to the fixture loaded from disk would not be tested.

test_trace_mutation_detection (test_mcp_compat.py:79) performs a deep-copy of the golden trace, mutates one field, and asserts inequality. This is an in-memory identity check, not a fixture-on-disk mutation test. A single byte change to golden/stub.jsonl that produces valid JSON would not be caught unless the byte change altered the `id` field tested here.

checks.name: Network-dependent harnesses: timeout enforcement and retry policy

findings.finding: devnet_roundtrip.py confirm_transaction() iterates `for _ in range(CONFIRM_TIMEOUT)` (30 iterations) but there is NO sleep between attempts — this is a busy-poll loop that will exhaust 30 iterations in microseconds, not 30 seconds. There is also no timeout on the RPC client.get_signature_status() HTTP call itself. In full mode this will either fail instantly or hang indefinitely on a slow RPC.

arweave_roundtrip.py wait_for_finalization() has the same busy-poll problem (FINALIZATION_TIMEOUT=60 loop with no sleep). requests.get() uses no explicit timeout parameter in the polling loop, only the upload step has `timeout=30`. A slow/hanging node will block the harness indefinitely.
No retry policy with backoff on 429/503 responses. The loop increments attempt count but does not implement exponential or linear backoff on rate-limit or server errors.

WASM fetch is simulated via HTTP-server (http-server on :3000). No network calls to external services, so timeout enforcement is not required for stub mode. The playwright webServer timeout is 120 s — acceptable.
No `timeout-minutes:` on any step in full-mode/action.yml. A hung RPC call could block the GitHub Actions runner indefinitely.

checks.name: Playwright: retry config and pinned browser version

findings.finding: playwright.config.ts sets `retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` — CI retry is present. Workers are serialized on CI (`workers: 1`). This is acceptable for flake reduction.

package.json pins `@playwright/test` to `^1.40.0` (caret range). This allows automatic minor/patch upgrades that can silently change the bundled browser binaries (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). The action.yml runs `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit` without specifying a version, meaning the installed browsers track whatever version ships with the resolved @playwright/test package. Browser version is NOT pinned.
No global `timeout:` set in playwright.config.ts — default Playwright test timeout is 30 s, which is reasonable but undeclared (implicit).

checks.name: Solana devnet rate-limit handling: backoff in full-mode

findings.finding: devnet_roundtrip.py has no HTTP 429 detection in any RPC call. confirm_transaction() and verify_on_devnet() use the solana-py Client which may raise exceptions on rate-limit but there is no retry-with-backoff wrapper. A single rate-limit response will either raise an unhandled exception (caught by the outer try/except and surfaced as RuntimeError) or return None/False immediately without retry.
No jitter in any retry or polling loop. Under concurrent CI runs (matrix builds) all instances would hammer the devnet RPC at the same cadence, amplifying rate-limit pressure.

checks.name: Independent verifier subprocess: timeout enforcement and non-zero exit propagation

findings.finding: independent_verifier.py correctly calls sys.exit(exit_code) with 0 on success and 1 on failure — exit propagation is correct.

action.yml invokes the verifier as a shell step (`python3 independent_verifier.py`) with no `timeout-minutes:`. If the verifier hangs (e.g., waiting on a real network call added in future), the step has no time bound.

The Makefile `verify` target does NOT invoke `verify-independent`. Only `make test` is called. The independent verifier is only executed via action.yml's explicit shell step. If someone runs `make verify` locally or in a non-action context, the independent verifier is skipped entirely.
Rust and TS serializer subprocess calls in test_byte_equivalence.py have `timeout=5` — this is adequate for local subprocesses.
All fixture JSON files are under 4 KB each (stub.json: ~20 bytes, stub-solana-tx.json: ~120 bytes, stub-arweave-tx.json: ~180 bytes, stub.jsonl: ~360 bytes). Well within the 100 KB threshold.

checks.name: Composite actions: artifact upload on failure for debugging

findings.finding: action.yml uploads artifact `byte-equivalence-report` with `if: always()` — present and correct.

action.yml uploads artifact `full-mode-report` with `if: always()` — present. However, the upload path is `fabric/harnesses/full-mode/` which includes source files but not necessarily pytest XML/HTML reports (no `--junitxml` flag passed to pytest). Test result files are not explicitly generated.
action.yml uploads `mcp-compat-report` with `if: always()` — present. Same observation about missing explicit pytest report output.
action.yml uploads `playwright-report/` directory with `if: always()` — Playwright generates HTML reports there by default. This is the correct path for Playwright.

top_issues: Mutation detection tests are cosmetic: they use Python hash() (non-deterministic) or in-memory object comparison, never re-running the actual serializers against mutated fixture data. A byte change on disk goes undetected.

Solana devnet confirm_transaction() and Arweave wait_for_finalization() are tight busy-poll loops with no sleep, no RPC call timeout, and no backoff — a rate-limit or slow node causes either instant false-failure or indefinite hang.
Serializer subprocess failures return None silently; test assertions are gated with `if result:`, allowing toolchain-build failures to produce green tests.
Playwright browser version not pinned: @playwright/test ^1.40.0 caret range allows browser binary upgrades that can introduce flakes.

word_summary: Four critical and eight high-severity issues found. Mutation detection tests are cosmetic—they compare in-memory hashes, never invoking serializers against mutated fixtures. Solana and Arweave polling loops are busy-polls with no sleep or RPC timeout, causing instant false-failure or indefinite hang under rate-limits. Serializer subprocess failures return None silently, letting toolchain breaks produce green exits. Playwright browser version is unpinned via caret range. The independent verifier is omitted from `make verify`, runs only via action.yml. Fixture sizes are all within limits; all four composite actions upload artifacts on failure.
